Cold Process.name: Lavender and Shea Butter Soap
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Ensure you have all ingredients and equipment ready.
2. Wear protective gear such as gloves and goggles.
3. Carefully add the lye to the distilled water while stirring. Set aside to cool.
4. Melt the shea butter, coconut oil, and olive oil together in a stainless steel pot.
5. Once the oils and lye solution are both around 100-110°F (38-43°C), pour the lye solution into the oils.
6. Use a stick blender to mix until it reaches trace (a pudding-like consistency).
7. Stir in the lavender essential oil until fully incorporated.
8. Pour the mixture into molds and tap to remove air bubbles.
9. Allow it to set for 24 hours.
10. After 24 hours, remove from molds and cut into bars.
11. Cure for 4-6 weeks in a well-ventilated area.
Cold Process.benefits: Lavender oil promotes relaxation and reduces stress. Shea butter moisturizes and nourishes the skin, providing relief for dryness and irritation. Olive oil and coconut oil hydrate and protect the skin, leaving it soft and supple.

Cold Process.name: Grapefruit and Bergamot Soap
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Dried Lavender Buds (optional, for exfoliation and decoration)
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Preparation: Same as Lavender and Shea Butter Soap.
2. Mixing Lye Solution: Same as Lavender and Shea Butter Soap.
3. Preparing Oils: Same as Lavender and Shea Butter Soap.
4. Combining Ingredients: Once the oils and lye solution are both around 100-110°F (38-43°C), pour the lye solution into the oils.
5. Use a stick blender to mix until it reaches trace.
6. Adding Essential Oils: Stir in the grapefruit essential oil and bergamot essential oil until fully incorporated.
7. Pouring and Setting: Same as Lavender and Shea Butter Soap.
8. Safety First: Put on your safety goggles and gloves. Work in a well-ventilated area.
9. Prepare the Lye Solution: Slowly add the sodium hydroxide to the distilled water (never the other way around) in a well-ventilated area. Stir until dissolved and set aside to cool.
10. Melt the Oils: Combine olive oil, coconut oil, shea butter, and castor oil in a large bowl. Gently heat until the shea butter and coconut oil are melted and the mixture is around 100°F (38°C).
11. Combine Lye and Oils: Once both the lye solution and the oils are approximately the same temperature (between 95°F and 105°F or 35°C and 40°C), slowly pour the lye solution into the oils while blending with a stick blender until trace is reached (when the mixture is thick enough to leave a visible trail when dripped on the surface).
12. Add Lavender and Colorant: Once trace is achieved, add the lavender essential oil and colorant (if using). Blend until just incorporated. If using lavender buds, you can either mix some in now or sprinkle them on top of the poured soap for decoration.
13. Pour into Mold: Pour the soap mixture into your mold. Tap the mold gently on the counter to remove any air bubbles.
14. Cure: Cover the mold with plastic wrap and wrap it in towels to insulate. After 24-48 hours, unmold the soap and cut it into bars. Cure the bars in a well-ventilated area on a rack for 4-6 weeks before using.

Cold Process.name: Tropical Coconut Bliss Soap
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Put on protective gear including gloves, goggles, and long sleeves.
2. In a well-ventilated area, carefully add the lye to the coconut milk, stirring until fully dissolved. Allow the mixture to cool.
3. Melt the coconut oil and shea butter in a double boiler until fully liquid.
4. Once the lye mixture and oils have cooled to around 110°F (43°C), slowly pour the lye mixture into the oils, stirring continuously.
5. Use a stick blender to mix until the soap reaches trace, where it thickens to the consistency of thin custard.
6. Add the coconut fragrance oil and blend thoroughly.
7. Pour the soap into molds and sprinkle dried coconut flakes on top if desired.
8. Allow the soap to cure in the molds for 24-48 hours, then unmold and cut into bars.
9. Cure the bars in a cool, dry place for 4-6 weeks before use.
Cold Process.benefits: Coconut oil moisturizes and nourishes the skin, leaving it soft and hydrated. Shea butter adds extra moisture and helps soothe dry, irritated skin. Olive oil contributes to a creamy lather and helps retain moisture. Coconut milk provides additional hydration and imparts a creamy texture to the soap. Coconut fragrance oil gives a tropical scent reminiscent of a day at the beach.

1. Prepare acai berry tea by brewing acai berries in hot water for 30 minutes, then strain and allow it to cool to room temperature.
2. Melt the olive oil, coconut oil, palm oil, and shea butter in a double boiler until fully liquid.
3. Once the lye mixture and oils have cooled to around 110°F (43°C), slowly pour the lye mixture into the oils, stirring continuously.
4. Use a stick blender to mix until the soap reaches trace.
5. Add the cooled acai berry tea and acai berry fragrance oil, and blend thoroughly.
6. If desired, add a small amount of acai berry powder for color and exfoliation and mix well.
7. Pour the soap into molds.
8. Allow the soap to cure and cut into bars.

8. Allow the soap to cure and then cut into bars.

Cold Process.name: Samoan Taro Root Soap
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Prepare taro root puree by cooking taro root until soft, then blending it with water until smooth. Allow it to cool to room temperature.
2. Melt the olive oil, coconut oil, palm oil, and shea butter in a double boiler until fully liquid.
3. Once the lye mixture and oils have cooled to around 110°F (43°C), slowly pour the lye mixture into the oils while stirring continuously.
4. Use a stick blender to mix until the soap reaches trace.
5. Add the cooled taro root puree and taro root fragrance oil, and blend thoroughly.
6. If desired, add a small amount of purple mica powder for color and mix well.
7. Pour the soap into molds.
8. Allow the soap to cure and then cut into bars.

Cold Process.name: Tropical Coconut Dream
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Melt the coconut oil and palm oil in a double boiler until fully liquid.
2. Once melted, add the olive oil and castor oil to the mixture.
3. In a separate container, mix the sodium hydroxide with the cooled coconut milk. Allow it to cool.
4. Once the lye mixture and oils have cooled to around 110°F (43°C), slowly pour the lye mixture into the oils while stirring continuously.
5. Use a stick blender to mix until the soap reaches trace.
6. Add the coconut fragrance oil, and blend thoroughly.
7. If desired, add a small amount of white mica powder for color and mix well.
8. Pour the soap into molds.
9. Allow the soap to cure and then cut into bars.

Cold Process.name: Lavender Fields Bliss
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Prepare lavender infusion by steeping dried lavender flowers in hot water for 30 minutes, then strain and allow it to cool to room temperature.
2. Melt the olive oil, coconut oil, palm oil, and shea butter in a double boiler until fully liquid.
3. Once the lye mixture and oils have cooled to around 110°F (43°C), slowly pour the lye mixture into the oils while stirring continuously.
4. Use a stick blender to mix until the soap reaches trace.
5. Add the cooled lavender infusion and lavender essential oil, and blend thoroughly.
6. If desired, add a small amount of purple mica powder for color and mix well.
7. Pour the soap into molds.
8. Allow the soap to cure and then cut into bars.

Cold Process.name: Citrus Burst Delight
ingredients: 150g citrus juice (combination of orange and lemon, cooled)
Orange and yellow mica powder (optional, for color)
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Zest oranges and lemons, then juice them. Allow the juice to cool to room temperature.
2. Melt the olive oil, coconut oil, palm oil, and shea butter in a double boiler until fully liquid.
3. Once the mixture and oils have cooled to around 110°F (43°C), slowly pour the lye mixture into the oils while stirring continuously.
4. Use a stick blender to mix until the soap reaches trace.
5. Add the cooled citrus juice, zest, and citrus essential oil blend, and blend thoroughly.
6. If desired, add a small amount of orange and yellow mica powder for color and mix well.
7. Pour the soap into molds. Allow the soap to cure and then cut into bars.

Cold Process.name: Peppermint Swirl Sensation
ingredients: Red and white mica powder (optional, for color)
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Prepare peppermint-infused water by steeping fresh peppermint leaves in hot water for 30 minutes, then strain and allow it to cool to room temperature.
2. Melt the coconut oil and palm oil in a double boiler until fully liquid.
3. Once melted, add the olive oil and castor oil to the mixture.
4. In a separate container, mix the sodium hydroxide with the cooled peppermint-infused water. Allow it to cool.
5. Once the lye mixture and oils have cooled to around 110°F (43°C), slowly pour the lye mixture into the oils while stirring continuously.
6. Use a stick blender to mix until the soap reaches trace.
7. Add the peppermint essential oil, and blend thoroughly.
8. Divide the soap mixture into two parts. Color one part with red mica powder and leave the other part uncolored.
9. Pour the uncolored soap into molds, then pour the red-colored soap in a swirling pattern on top.
10. Use a skewer to create swirls in the soap mixture.
11. Allow the soap to cure and then cut into bars.

Cold Process.name: Rose Garden Romance
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Prepare rose water by distilling fresh rose petals in water. Allow it to cool to room temperature.
2. Melt the olive oil, coconut oil, palm oil, and shea butter in a double boiler until fully liquid.
3. Once the lye mixture and oils have cooled to around 110°F (43°C), slowly pour the lye mixture into the oils while stirring continuously.
4. Use a stick blender to mix until the soap reaches trace.
5. Add the cooled rose water and rose essential oil, and blend thoroughly.
6. If desired, add a small amount of pink mica powder for color and mix well.
7. Pour the soap into molds.
8. Optionally, sprinkle dried rose petals on top of the soap for decoration.
9. Allow the soap to cure and then cut into bars.

Cold Process.name: Eucalyptus Forest Freshness
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Prepare eucalyptus-infused water by steeping eucalyptus leaves in hot water for 30 minutes, then strain and allow it to cool to room temperature.
2. Melt the olive oil, coconut oil, palm oil, and shea butter in a double boiler until fully liquid.
3. Once the lye mixture and oils have cooled to around 110°F (43°C), slowly pour the lye mixture into the oils while stirring continuously.
4. Use a stick blender to mix until the soap reaches trace.
5. Add the cooled eucalyptus-infused water and eucalyptus essential oil, and blend thoroughly.
6. If desired, add a small amount of green mica powder for color and mix well.
7. Pour the soap into molds.
8. Allow the soap to cure and then cut into bars.

Cold Process.name: Honey Almond Harmony
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Melt the olive oil, coconut oil, palm oil, and sweet almond oil in a double boiler until fully liquid.
2. Once melted, add the cooled honey to the mixture and stir well.
3. In a separate container, mix the sodium hydroxide with water. Allow it to cool.
4. Once the lye mixture and oils have cooled to around 110°F (43°C), slowly pour the lye mixture into the oils while stirring continuously.
5. Use a stick blender to mix until the soap reaches trace.
6. Add the almond fragrance oil, and blend thoroughly.
7. If desired, add a small amount of yellow mica powder for color and mix well.
8. Pour the soap into molds.
9. Allow the soap to cure and then cut into bars.

Cold Process.name: Jasmine Blossom Serenity
ingredients: White and yellow mica powder (optional, for color)
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Prepare jasmine tea by steeping jasmine flowers in hot water for 30 minutes, then strain and allow it to cool to room temperature.
2. Melt the olive oil, coconut oil, palm oil, and shea butter in a double boiler until fully liquid.
3. Oncemmthe lye mixture and oils have cooled to around 110°F (43°C), slowly pour the lye mixture into the oils while stirring continuously.
4. Use a stick blender to mix until the soap reaches trace.
5. Add the cooled jasmine tea and jasmine fragrance oil, and blend thoroughly.
6. If desired, divide the soap batter into two parts. Add white mica powder to one part and yellow mica powder to the other part, mixing each thoroughly.
7. Pour the white-colored soap into molds, then pour the yellow-colored soap on top in a swirling pattern.
8. Use a skewer to create swirls in the soap mixture.Allow the soap to cure and then cut into bars.

Cold Process.name: Ocean Breeze Escape
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Prepare seawater by filtering ocean water and allowing it to cool to room temperature.
2. Melt the olive oil, coconut oil, palm oil, and shea butter in a double boiler until fully liquid.
3. Once the lye mixture and oils have cooled to around 110°F (43°C), slowly pour the lye mixture into the oils while stirring continuously.
4. Use a stick blender to mix until the soap reaches trace.
5. Add the cooled seawater and ocean breeze fragrance oil, and blend thoroughly.
6. If desired, add a small amount of blue mica powder for color and mix well.
7. Pour the soap into molds.
8. Allow the soap to cure and then cut into bars.

Cold Process.name: Lemongrass Citrus Zest
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Prepare lemongrass-infused water by steeping lemongrass in hot water for 30 minutes, then strain and allow it to cool to room temperature.
2. Melt the olive oil, coconut oil, palm oil, and shea butter in a double boiler until fully liquid.
3. Once the lye mixture and oils have cooled to around 110°F (43°C), slowly pour the lye mixture into the oils while stirring continuously.
4. Use a stick blender to mix until the soap reaches trace.
5. Add the cooled lemongrass-infused water, lemongrass essential oil, and zest of lemons and limes. Blend thoroughly.
6. Pour the soap mixture into molds.
7. Allow the soap to cure for about 24-48 hours, then unmold and cut it into bars.
8. Let the bars cure for an additional 4-6 weeks in a well-ventilated area before using.

Cold Process.name: Vanilla Bean Velvet
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Prepare vanilla bean infusion by steeping vanilla beans in hot water for 30 minutes, then strain and allow it to cool to room temperature.
2. Melt the olive oil, coconut oil, palm oil, and shea butter in a double boiler until fully liquid.
3. Once the lye mixture and oils have cooled to around 110°F (43°C), slowly pour the lye mixture into the oils while stirring continuously.
4. Use a stick blender to mix until the soap reaches trace.
5. Add the cooled vanilla bean infusion, vanilla fragrance oil, and vanilla bean seeds (if using). Blend thoroughly.
6. Pour the soap mixture into molds.
7. Allow the soap to cure for about 24-48 hours, then unmold and cut it into bars.
8. Let the bars cure for an additional 4-6 weeks in a well-ventilated area before using.

Cold Process.name: Sandalwood Serenade
ingredients: Red and yellow mica powder (optional, for color)
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Prepare sandalwood-infused oil by steeping sandalwood chips in a carrier oil (such as olive oil) for several weeks. Strain and allow it to cool to room temperature.
2. Melt the olive oil, coconut oil, palm oil, and shea butter in a double boiler until fully liquid.
3. Once the lye mixture and oils have cooled to around 110°F (43°C), slowly pour the lye mixture into the oils while stirring continuously.
4. Use a stick blender to mix until the soap reaches trace.
5. Add the cooled sandalwood-infused oil and sandalwood fragrance oil. Blend thoroughly.
6. If desired, add a small amount of red and yellow mica powder for color and mix well.
7. Pour the soap mixture into molds.
8. Allow the soap to cure for about 24-48 hours, then unmold and cut it into bars.Let the bars cure for an additional 4-6 weeks in a well-ventilated area before using.

Cold Process.name: Tea Tree Tingle
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Prepare tea tree-infused water by steeping tea tree leaves in hot water for 30 minutes, then strain and allow it to cool to room temperature.
2. Melt the olive oil, coconut oil, palm oil, and shea butter in a double boiler until fully liquid.
3. Once the lye mixture and oils have cooled to around 110°F (43°C), slowly pour the lye mixture into the oils while stirring continuously.
4. Use a stick blender to mix until the soap reaches trace.
5. Add the cooled tea tree-infused water and tea tree essential oil. Blend thoroughly.
6. If desired, add a small amount of green mica powder for color and mix well.
7. Pour the soap mixture into molds.
8. Allow the soap to cure for about 24-48 hours, then unmold and cut it into bars.
9. Let the bars cure for an additional 4-6 weeks in a well-ventilated area before using.

Cold Process.name: Cucumber Mint Refresher
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Wash the cucumber thoroughly and cut it into slices.
2. In a blender, combine cucumber slices, fresh mint leaves, and water. Blend until smooth.
3. Strain the mixture through a fine mesh sieve to remove any pulp.
4. Taste the liquid and add honey or sugar if desired for sweetness.
5. Pour the cucumber mint juice into glasses filled with ice cubes.
6. Garnish with lemon slices if desired.
7. Serve immediately and enjoy the refreshing drink!

Cold Process.name: Patchouli Paradise
ingredients: Few drops of patchouli essential oil (food-grade)
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, combine coconut water, pineapple juice, orange juice, and honey. Stir well until honey is dissolved.
2. Add a few drops of patchouli essential oil and mix thoroughly.
3. Chill the drink in the refrigerator for at least an hour.
4. Serve over ice and garnish with pineapple slices if desired.
5. Enjoy the tropical paradise flavor of Patchouli Paradise!

Cold Process.name: Aloe Vera Soothe
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, mix together aloe vera juice, cucumber juice, apple juice, and lemon juice.
2. Taste the mixture and add honey or agave syrup for sweetness if desired.
3. Stir well until the sweetener is fully incorporated.
4. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the aloe vera mixture over the ice.
5. Serve immediately to enjoy the soothing goodness of Aloe Vera Soothe!

Cold Process.name: Bergamot Bliss
ingredients: Few drops of bergamot essential oil (food-grade)
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, combine brewed green tea, lemon juice, and honey.
2. Stir until the honey is dissolved.
3. Add a few drops of bergamot essential oil and mix well.
4. Chill the tea mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
5. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled bergamot green tea over the ice.
6. Garnish with lemon slices if desired.
7. Serve and savor the refreshing and citrusy flavor of Bergamot Bliss!

Cold Process.name: Pineapple Passion
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a blender, combine pineapple juice, coconut milk, lime juice, and honey (if using).
2. Blend until smooth and well combined.
3. Taste the mixture and adjust sweetness according to preference by adding more honey if needed.
4. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the pineapple passion mixture over the ice.
5. Garnish each glass with a pineapple wedge if desired.
6. Serve immediately and enjoy the tropical delight of Pineapple Passion!

Cold Process.name: Cherry Blossom Whisper
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, combine cherry juice, sparkling water, lime juice, and honey.
2. Stir until the honey is dissolved and all ingredients are well mixed.
3. Taste and adjust sweetness if needed by adding more honey.
4. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the cherry blossom mixture over the ice.
5. Garnish each glass with fresh cherries if desired.
6. Serve immediately and enjoy the delicate flavor of Cherry Blossom Whisper!

Cold Process.name: Oatmeal Honey Soothing
ingredients: 2 cups almond milk (or any milk of your choice)
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a saucepan, heat almond milk over medium heat until warm but not boiling.
2. Stir in rolled oats and let them simmer for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
3. Remove from heat and stir in honey, vanilla extract, and cinnamon (if using).
4. Allow the mixture to cool slightly.
5. Pour the oatmeal honey mixture into a blender and blend until smooth.
6. Strain the mixture through a fine mesh sieve to remove any oatmeal residue.
7. Chill the oatmeal honey mixture in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
8. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
9. Serve and enjoy the comforting and soothing taste of Oatmeal Honey Soothing!

Cold Process.name: Frankincense Fusion
ingredients: Few drops of frankincense essential oil (food-grade)
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, mix together coconut water, pineapple juice, orange juice, and honey.
2. Stir until the honey is dissolved and all ingredients are well combined.
3. Add a few drops of frankincense essential oil and mix thoroughly.
4. Chill the drink in the refrigerator for at least an hour.
5. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the frankincense fusion over the ice.
6. Garnish each glass with an orange slice if desired.
7. Serve and enjoy the unique and exotic flavor of Frankincense Fusion!

Cold Process.name: Blackberry Sage Sensation
ingredients: Fresh blackberries and sage leaves for garnish (optional)
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a saucepan, combine blackberries, sage leaves, and water.
2. Bring the mixture to a simmer over medium heat and let it simmer for about 10 minutes.
3. Remove from heat and allow the mixture to cool slightly.
4. Strain the liquid through a fine mesh sieve, pressing the blackberries and sage leaves to extract all the juice.
5. Discard the solids and stir in honey or sugar if desired.
6. Chill the blackberry sage mixture in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
7. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
8. Garnish each glass with fresh blackberries and sage leaves if desired.
9. Serve and enjoy the delightful blend of flavors in Blackberry Sage Sensation!

Cold Process.name: Mango Tango Temptation
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a blender, combine mango chunks, orange juice, coconut water, lime juice, and honey.
2. Blend until smooth and well combined.
3. Taste the mixture and adjust sweetness if needed by adding more honey.
4. Chill the mango tango mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
5. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
6. Garnish each glass with a slice of mango if desired.
7. Serve and enjoy the tropical delight of Mango Tango Temptation!

Cold Process.name: Neroli Nirvana
ingredients: Few drops of neroli essential oil (food-grade)
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, combine brewed chamomile tea, honey, and orange juice.
2. Stir until the honey is dissolved.
3. Add a few drops of neroli essential oil and mix well.
4. Chill the neroli nirvana tea in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
5. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled tea over the ice.
6. Garnish each glass with a sprinkle of orange zest if desired.
7. Serve and enjoy the calming and fragrant experience of Neroli Nirvana!

Cold Process.name: Green Tea Zen
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, mix together brewed green tea, honey, and lemon juice.
2. Stir until the honey is dissolved and all ingredients are well combined.
3. Chill the green tea mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
4. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled green tea over the ice.
5. Garnish each glass with a lemon slice and a mint leaf if desired.
6. Serve and enjoy the refreshing and revitalizing taste of Green Tea Zen!

Cold Process.name: Chamomile Calm
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, mix together brewed chamomile tea, honey, and lemon juice.
2. Stir until the honey is dissolved and all ingredients are well combined.
3. Chill the chamomile mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
4. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled chamomile tea over the ice.
5. Garnish each glass with a lemon slice and a few chamomile flowers if desired.
6. Serve and enjoy the soothing and calming effects of Chamomile Calm!

Cold Process.name: Pomegranate Paradise
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, combine pomegranate juice, cranberry juice, sparkling water, and lime juice.
2. Stir until all ingredients are well mixed.
3. Chill the pomegranate paradise mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
4. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
5. Garnish each glass with a few pomegranate arils if desired.
6. Serve and enjoy the vibrant and refreshing taste of Pomegranate Paradise!

Cold Process.name: Lemongrass Sage Serenity
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a saucepan, combine coconut water, lemon juice, honey, chopped lemongrass, and chopped sage leaves.
2. Bring the mixture to a simmer over medium heat and let it simmer for about 5 minutes.
3. Remove from heat and let it cool completely.
4. Strain the mixture through a fine mesh sieve to remove the lemongrass and sage leaves.
5. Chill the lemongrass sage mixture in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
6. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
7. Garnish each glass with a lemon slice if desired.
8. Serve and enjoy the serene and refreshing flavor of Lemongrass Sage Serenity!

Cold Process.name: Coconut Lime Delight
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, combine coconut water, coconut milk, lime juice, and honey.
2. Stir until the honey is dissolved and all ingredients are well combined.
3. Chill the coconut lime mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
4. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
5. Garnish each glass with a lime slice and a sprinkle of shredded coconut if desired.
6. Serve and enjoy the tropical and refreshing taste of Coconut Lime Delight!

Cold Process.name: Gingerbread Joy
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a saucepan, heat the milk over medium heat until warm.
2. Stir in molasses, ground ginger, ground cinnamon, ground nutmeg, and ground cloves.
3. Whisk continuously until all ingredients are well combined and the mixture is heated through.
4. Remove from heat and pour into mugs.
5. Top with whipped cream and sprinkle with ground cinnamon if desired.
6. Serve immediately and enjoy the cozy and comforting flavor of Gingerbread Joy!

Cold Process.name: Lavender Vanilla Tranquility
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a saucepan, heat the milk over medium heat until warm but not boiling.
2. Add dried lavender buds to the warm milk and let it steep for about 5 minutes.
3. Strain the lavender-infused milk into another saucepan, discarding the lavender buds.
4. Stir in vanilla extract and honey until well combined.
5. Heat the mixture until it reaches your desired temperature.
6. Pour into mugs and garnish with lavender sprigs if desired.
7. Serve and enjoy the calming and aromatic Lavender Vanilla Tranquility!

Cold Process.name: Cedarwood Comfort
ingredients: 2 cups almond milk (or any milk of your choice)
Cedarwood essential oil (food-grade, a few drops)
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a saucepan, heat the almond milk over medium heat until warm but not boiling.
2. Stir in ground cinnamon, ground nutmeg, ground cloves, vanilla extract, and maple syrup.
3. Add a few drops of cedarwood essential oil and stir well.
4. Heat the mixture until it reaches your desired temperature.
5. Pour into mugs and serve immediately.
6. Enjoy the cozy and comforting flavor of Cedarwood Comfort!

Cold Process.name: Peony Petals Perfection
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, combine brewed hibiscus tea, cranberry juice, orange juice, and honey.
2. Stir until the honey is dissolved and all ingredients are well mixed.
3. Chill the peony petals mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
4. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
5. Garnish each glass with edible flowers if desired.
6. Serve and enjoy the floral and refreshing taste of Peony Petals Perfection!

Cold Process.name: Bergamot Basil Bliss
ingredients: Few drops of bergamot essential oil (food-grade)
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, mix together brewed green tea, lemon juice, and honey.
2. Stir until the honey is dissolved.
3. Add a few drops of bergamot essential oil and mix well.
4. Chill the bergamot basil mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
5. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled tea over the ice.
6. Garnish each glass with fresh basil leaves if desired.
7. Serve and enjoy the citrusy and aromatic flavor of Bergamot Basil Bliss!

Cold Process.name: Orange Blossom Oasis
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, combine freshly squeezed orange juice, coconut water, and honey.
2. Stir until the honey is dissolved and all ingredients are well mixed.
3. Chill the orange blossom mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
4. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
5. Garnish each glass with orange slices if desired.
6. Serve and enjoy the refreshing and citrusy taste of Orange Blossom Oasis!

Cold Process.name: Cinnamon Spice Delight
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a saucepan, heat the milk over medium heat.
2. Add cinnamon sticks, maple syrup, ground cinnamon, and ground nutmeg.
3. Stir continuously until the mixture is heated through and aromatic.
4. Remove from heat and let it steep for a few minutes.
5. Remove the cinnamon sticks and pour the mixture into mugs.
6. Top with whipped cream and sprinkle with ground cinnamon if desired.
7. Serve immediately and enjoy the cozy and comforting flavor of Cinnamon Spice Delight!

Cold Process.name: Juniper Berry Jubilee
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, combine sparkling water, juniper berry syrup, and lime juice.
2. Stir until well mixed.
3. Chill the juniper berry jubilee mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
4. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
5. Garnish each glass with a lime slice and a few juniper berries if desired.
6. Serve and enjoy the festive and refreshing flavor of Juniper Berry Jubilee!

Cold Process.name: Lavender Lemongrass Love
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, mix together brewed lemongrass tea, lavender syrup, and lemon juice.
2. Stir until well combined.
3. Chill the lavender lemongrass mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
4. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
5. Garnish each glass with fresh lavender sprigs if desired.
6. Serve and enjoy the harmonious blend of Lavender Lemongrass Love!

Cold Process.name: Cranberry Cinnamon Sensation
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, combine cranberry juice, orange juice, apple cider, and ground cinnamon.
2. Stir until well mixed.
3. Chill the cranberry cinnamon mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
4. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
5. Garnish each glass with an orange slice and a cinnamon stick if desired.
6. Serve and enjoy the festive and flavorful Cranberry Cinnamon Sensation!

Cold Process.name: Jasmine Rose Revival
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, mix together brewed jasmine tea, rose water, and honey.
2. Stir until the honey is dissolved and all ingredients are well combined.
3. Chill the jasmine rose mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
4. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
5. Garnish each glass with fresh rose petals if desired.
6. Serve and enjoy the delicate and floral taste of Jasmine Rose Revival!

Cold Process.name: Grapefruit Guava Glamour
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, combine grapefruit juice, guava juice, sparkling water, and honey.
2. Stir until the honey is dissolved and all ingredients are well mixed.
3. Chill the grapefruit guava mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
4. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
5. Garnish each glass with a slice of grapefruit if desired.
6. Serve and enjoy the refreshing and exotic flavor of Grapefruit Guava Glamour!

Cold Process.name: Honey Lavender Luxe
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a saucepan, heat the milk over medium heat until warm but not boiling.
2. Add dried lavender buds to the warm milk and let it steep for about 5 minutes.
3. Strain the lavender-infused milk into another saucepan, discarding the lavender buds.
4. Stir in honey and vanilla extract until well combined.
5. Heat the mixture until it reaches your desired temperature.
6. Pour into mugs and garnish with lavender sprigs if desired.
7. Serve and enjoy the luxurious and soothing taste of Honey Lavender Luxe!

Cold Process.name: Ylang Ylang Yawn
ingredients: Few drops of ylang ylang essential oil (food-grade)
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, combine chamomile tea, honey, vanilla extract, and ylang ylang essential oil.
2. Stir until the honey is dissolved and all ingredients are well mixed.
3. Chill the ylang ylang yawn mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
4. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
5. Garnish each glass with a lemon slice if desired.
6. Serve and enjoy the calming and aromatic flavor of Ylang Ylang Yawn!

Cold Process.name: Lavender Lemon Lullaby
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a saucepan, bring water to a boil.
2. Remove from heat and add dried lavender buds to the hot water.
3. Let the lavender steep for about 10 minutes.
4. Strain the lavender-infused water into a pitcher, discarding the lavender buds.
5. Stir in lemon juice and honey until well combined.
6. Chill the lavender lemon lullaby mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
7. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
8. Garnish each glass with a lemon slice if desired.
9. Serve and enjoy the soothing and refreshing taste of Lavender Lemon Lullaby!

Cold Process.name: Sandalwood Rose Romance
ingredients: 2 cups almond milk (or any milk of your choice)
Few drops of sandalwood essential oil (food-grade)
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a saucepan, heat the almond milk over medium heat until warm but not boiling.
2. Stir in ground cardamom, ground nutmeg, rose water, and honey until well combined.
3. Add a few drops of sandalwood essential oil and stir again.
4. Heat the mixture until it reaches your desired temperature.
5. Pour into mugs and garnish with dried rose petals if desired.
6. Serve and enjoy the romantic and aromatic flavor of Sandalwood Rose Romance!

Cold Process.name: Coconut Papaya Paradise
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a pitcher, combine coconut water, papaya juice, pineapple juice, lime juice, and honey.
2. Stir until the honey is dissolved and all ingredients are well mixed.
3. Chill the coconut papaya mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
4. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
5. Garnish each glass with a slice of papaya if desired.

Cold Process.name: Sweet Orange Sunshine

4. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
5. Garnish each glass with an orange slice if desired.

2. Stir in ground cinnamon, ground nutmeg, honey, and vanilla extract until well combined.
3. Add a few drops of patchouli essential oil and stir again.
4. Heat the mixture until it reaches your desired temperature.

Cold Process.name: Minty Melon Madness

2. Blend until smooth.
3. Strain the mixture through a fine mesh sieve to remove any pulp.
4. Taste the liquid and add honey or agave syrup if desired for sweetness.
5. Pour the minty melon juice into glasses filled with ice cubes.
6. Garnish with mint sprigs if desired.

Cold Process.name: Bergamot Mint Bliss

Cold Process.name: Lemongrass Ginger Glow
Cold Process.instructions:
1. In a saucepan, bring water to a boil.
2. Add chopped lemongrass and grated ginger to the boiling water.
3. Reduce the heat and let it simmer for about 10 minutes.
4. Remove from heat and strain the liquid into a pitcher to remove the lemongrass and ginger.
5. Stir in honey and lemon juice until well combined.
6. Chill the lemongrass ginger mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
7. Fill glasses with ice cubes and pour the chilled mixture over the ice.
8. Garnish each glass with a lemongrass stalk if desired.
9. Serve and enjoy the zesty and refreshing taste of Lemongrass Ginger Glow!

Cold Process.name: Rosemary Mint Magic

Cold Process.name: Olive Oil Delight Soap
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Put on safety gear including gloves, goggles, and long sleeves. Ensure proper ventilation.
2. In a well-ventilated area, carefully mix sodium hydroxide into distilled water. Allow it to cool.
3. In a double boiler, melt olive oil, coconut oil, and shea butter together until fully liquid.
4. Once both the lye mixture and oils are around 40-50°C, slowly pour the lye mixture into the oils.
5. Use a stick blender to blend the mixture until it reaches trace, resembling thin custard.
6. Add any optional essential oils or fragrance blend, if desired, and mix thoroughly.
7. Pour the soap batter into molds and cover with a towel or cardboard to insulate.

Cold Process.name: Olive Oil Soap
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Preparation: Prepare your mold for the soap batter. If you are using a wooden mold without a liner, line it with freezer paper or parchment paper. Cover your work area with newspaper or a protective surface. Make sure your equipment is clean and dry. Put on safety goggles and gloves.
2. Mix the lye solution: Wear a face mask and avoid inhaling the fumes from the lye solution. Weigh 215 grams or 7.58 ounces of distilled water in a heat-resistant container. Carefully weigh 107 grams or 3.7 ounces of lye (sodium hydroxide) in a separate container. Slowly add the lye to the water (never the other way around) while stirring gently until completely dissolved. The mixture will heat up (as high as 93+ C or 200+ C) and release eye, nose, throat and lung irritating fumes, so do this in a well-ventilated area, under a fume hood or even outside. Set the lye solution aside to cool to about 38-43°C (100-110°F). You may remove face mask at this point
3. Prepare the oils: Weigh 835 grams of olive oil in a separate container. Heat the olive oil in a saucepan or microwave until it reaches the same temperature range as the lye solution (38-43°C or 100-110°F). Use 30 second bursts in the microwave or low heat in the sauce pan to avoid scorching the oil. Or wait for the lye solution to cool enough reach the temperature of your olive oil.
4. Combine lye and oil: When both the lye water solution and the oils are the same temperature or between 90- and 1050 F or 32.22 to 40.50 C, slowly pour the lye solution into the olive oil while stirring continuously.
5. Mix soap batter to emulsion and trace: Use an immersion blender to mix the solution. Stick blend in 5-10 second bursts alternating with stirring with the stick blender or a spatula until it reaches "trace." Trace is achieved when the mixture is completely blended and no more oils float on the batter. The batter thickens and leaves a slightly visible trail or "trace" on the surface when dripped from the blender.
6. Add essential oils (optional): If you wish to add fragrance, now is the time to mix in your essential oils. Stir well to incorporate. Stir or stick blend until no trace of unincorporated oil is visible.
7. Pour into mold: Pour the soap mixture into your mold. If using a wooden mold, make sure it is lined with parchment or freezer paper first. Tap the mold gently on the counter to remove any air bubbles.
8. Insulate and cure: Cover the mold with a lid or cardboard and wrap it in a towel to insulate. Leave the soap undisturbed for 48 - 56 hours.
9. Unmold and cut: After at least 48 hours, check the soap. If using a wooden mold remove inner loaf of soap still enclosed in Parchment of freezer paper or a silicone mold, gently pull a small section of the paper or silicone away from one side. If batter sticks to the paper or mold, set aside for another 24 hours. When the sides come away cleanly, unmold the soap. If it's still soft, let it sit for another day or two before cutting. Once firm, cut the soap into bars using a Stainless-steel knife or soap cutter.
10. Drying: Place the bars on a drying rack in a well-ventilated area. Allow the soap to dry for 4-6 weeks, turning the bars occasionally to ensure even drying.
11. Storage: After drying, store your soap bars in a cool, dry place. Your homemade Olive Oil Soap is now ready to use!
Cold Process.source: Easy Soap Academy - 32 Cold Process Recipes
Cold Process.benefits: moisturizing and gentle on the skin

Cold Process.name: Honey Soap
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Preparation: Prepare soap mold. If using a wooden mold, line with freezer paper or parchment paper, Cover your work area with newspaper or a protective surface. Make sure your equipment is clean and dry. Put on safety goggles and gloves.
2. Mix the lye solution: Wear a face mask and avoid inhaling the fumes from the lye solution. Weigh 235 grams (8.3 ounces) of distilled water in a heat-resistant container. Carefully weigh 117 grams (4.15 ounces) of sodium hydroxide in a separate container. Slowly add the sodium hydroxide to the water (never the other way around) while stirring gently until completely dissolved. The mixture will heat up (as high as 93+ C or 200+ C) and release eye, nose, throat and lung irritating fumes, so do this in a well-ventilated area or under a fume hood. Set the lye solution aside to cool to about 38-43°C (100-110°F). You can remove your face mask at this point
3. Prepare the oils: Weigh 418 grams (14.7 ounces) of olive oil and 42 grams (1.5 ounces) of castor oil in a separate container. Always add the castor oil last as it is heavy and may stick to the container rather than mixing with the oil if added first.
4. Melt 209 grams (7.4 ounces) of coconut oil and 167 grams (5.9 ounces) of palm oil in a saucepan (double boiler) or microwave until it reaches the same temperature range as the lye solution (38-43°C or 100-110°F). Use 30 second bursts in the microwave or low heat in the sauce pan to avoid scorching the oil. Combine the melted oils and the liquid oils in mixing jug. Gently heat the honey by combining with like amount of hot water. This will make it more fluid and easier to distribute through the oils. Mix thoroughly into the warm oils.
5. Combine lye-water solution and oils: Slowly pour the lye-water solution into the oils while stirring continuously. Use an immersion blender to mix the solution. Stick blend in 5-10 second bursts alternating with stirring with the stick blender or a spatula until it reaches "trace." Trace is achieved when the mixture is completely blended and no more oils float on the batter. The batter thickens and leaves a slightly visible trail or "trace" on the surface when dripped from the blender.
6. Add essential oils or fragrance oils (optional): If you wish to add fragrance, now is the time to mix in your essential or fragrance oils. Hand-stir well to incorporate without accelerating trace. Stir until no trace of unincorporated oil is visible.
7. Pour into mold: Pour the soap mixture into your mold. If using a wooden mold, make sure it is lined with parchment paper first. Tap the mold gently on the counter to remove any air bubbles.
8. Refrigerate and cure: Cover the mold loosely with plastic film or parchment paper and place in the refrigerator You can remove from refrigerator after 8 – 12 hours. Leave the soap undisturbed for an additional 24-48 hours.
9. Unmold and cut: After 18 - 24 hours, check the soap. If using a wooden mold remove inner loaf of soap still enclosed in Parchment of freezer paper or a silicone mold, gently pull a small section of the paper or silicone away from one side. If batter sticks to the paper or mold, set aside for another 24 hours. When the sides come away cleanly, unmold the soap. If it's still soft, let it sit for another day or two before cutting. Once firm, cut the soap into bars using a Stainless-steel knife or soap cutter.
10. Drying: Place the bars on a drying rack in a well-ventilated area. Allow the soap to dry for 4-6 weeks, turning the bars occasionally to ensure even drying.
11. Storage: After drying, store your soap bars in a cool, dry place. Your homemade Honey Soap is now ready to use!

Cold Process.name: Eucalyptus Soap
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Preparation: Prepare soap mold. If using a wooden mold, line with freezer paper or parchment paper, Cover your work area with newspaper or a protective surface. Make sure your equipment is clean and dry. Put on safety goggles and gloves.
2. Mix the Essential Oil or Fragrance Oil with Dry Ingredients Choose the strength of the scent you wish to use from the ingredients list. In a clean glass container weigh out the essential oil or fragrance oil Add 2 Tablespoons of White Kaolin Clay and your choice of green colorants and mix thoroughly. Set aside to merge the ingredients.
3. Mix the lye solution: Wear a face mask and avoid inhaling the fumes from the lye solution. Weigh 233 grams (8.2 ounces) of chilled distilled water or distilled water ice cubes in a heat-resistant container. Carefully weigh 116 grams (4.1 ounces) of sodium hydroxide in a separate container. Slowly add the sodium hydroxide to the water or ice (never the other way around) while stirring gently until completely dissolved. The mixture will heat up (as high as 93+ C or 200+ C) and release eye, nose, throat and lung irritating fumes, so do this in a well-ventilated area or under a fume hood or outside.. Set the lye solution aside to cool to about 38-43°C (100-110°F).
4. Prepare the oils: Melt 206 grams (7.3 ounces) of coconut oil and 165 grams (5.8 ounces) of palm oil in a saucepan (double boiler) or microwave until it reaches the same temperature range as the lye solution (38-43°C or 100-110°F). Use 30 second bursts in the microwave or low heat in the sauce pan to avoid scorching the oil. Weigh 412 grams (14.6 ounces) of olive oil and 41 grams (1.5 ounces) of castor oil in a separate container. Always add the castor oil last as it is heavy and may stick to the container rather than mixing with the oil if added first. Combine the melted oils and the liquid oils in mixing jug. Mix thoroughly with whisk, spatula or stick blender to combine.
5. Combine lye-water solution and oils: Slowly pour the lye-water solution into the oils while stirring continuously. Use an immersion blender to mix the solution. Stick blend in 5-10 second bursts alternating with stirring with the stick blender or a spatula until it just reaches "trace." Trace is achieved when the mixture is completely blended and no more oils float on the batter. The batter thickens and leaves a slightly visible trail or "trace" on the surface when dripped from the blender. This can take as little as 30 seconds.
6. Add Fragrance (essential/fragrance oil), colorant, clay mixture from Step 2: Hand-stir well with spatula or long handle spoon to incorporate without further accelerating trace. Stir until no trace of unincorporated oil is visible.
7. Pour into mold: Pour the soap mixture into your mold. If using a wooden mold, make sure it is lined with parchment paper first. Tap the mold gently on the counter to remove any air bubbles. Optional decorative elements: Let the batter set up a little. While the surface is still ‘wet”, sprinkle dry, crushed Eucalyptus Leaves on top of the batter for decoration. A line down one side or the middle of the loaf is more appealing than completely covering the top.
8. Dry: Cover the mold loosely with plastic film or parchment paper and then cover with a towel to insulate. Leave the soap undisturbed for 18 - 24 hours.
9. Unmold and cut: After 18 - 24 hours, check the soap. If using a wooden mold remove inner loaf of soap still enclosed in Parchment of freezer paper or a silicone mold, gently pull a small section of the paper or silicone away from one side. If batter sticks to the paper or mold, set aside for another 24 hours. When the sides come away cleanly, unmold the soap. If it's still soft, let it sit for another day or two before cutting. Once firm, cut the soap into bars using a Stainless-steel knife or soap cutter.
10. Drying: Place the bars on a drying rack in a well-ventilated area. Allow the soap to dry for 4-6 weeks, turning the bars occasionally to ensure even drying.
11. Storage: After drying, store your soap bars in a cool, dry place. Your homemade Eucalyptus Soap is ready to use!

Cold Process.name: Lavender Soap
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Preparation: Prepare mold. If using a wooden mold, line with freezer or parchment paper. Cover your work area with newspaper or a protective surface. Ensure your equipment is clean and dry. Put on safety goggles and gloves.
2. Mix the lye solution: Wear a face mask and avoid inhaling the fumes from the lye solution. Weigh 235 grams of distilled water into a heat-resistant container. Carefully add 117 grams of lye to the water while stirring gently. The mixture will heat up and release fumes, so do this in a well-ventilated area or under a fume hood. Set the lye solution aside to cool to about 38-43°C (100-110°F). You can safely remove your mask at this time
3. Prepare the Essential Oil blend In glass or stainless-steel container add 2 T white Kaolin Clay, Purple Clay or Mica and 25 grams of Lavender Essential Oil. Blend thoroughly. If necessary, add a small amount of olive oil to make a smooth paste. This helps anchor the fragrance as well as avoid speckles in the color.
4. Prepare the oils: Melt 209 grams (7.36 ounces) coconut oil and 167 grams (5.89 ounces) palm oil in microwave or double boiler. Use 30 second bursts in the microwave or low heat under the double boiler to avoid over heating the oils. Weigh 417.5 grams (14.7 ounces) of olive oil and 41.75 grams (1.47 ounces) of Castor Oil into large container suitable for mixing total batch. Always add Castor Oil last as it is heavy and needs to blend with oils rather than stick to container. Add melted oils to container containing Olive oil and Castor Oil. Add 1 – 2 teaspoons sugar.
5. Combine lye solution and oils: Check temperature of lye solution. When lye solution and oils are in the correct temperature range (38-43°C or 100-110°F) they are ready to combine. Slowly pour the lye solution into the oils while stirring continuously with whisk, spatula or shaft of immersion blender. Use an immersion blender to mix the solution until it reaches "trace." Mix in 5 second bursts, stirring well between bursts. Move slowly as you learn how the batter reacts. Trace is achieved when all of the oils are incorporated and the mixture thickens slightly – about the consistency of pancake or crepe batter. It will leave a visible trail or "trace" on the surface when dripped from the blender.
6. Add lavender essential oil, clay mixture and optional ground dried lavender buds: Add the mixture of clays and lavender essential oil to the mixture and hand stir well to incorporate and blend color. Use a whisk, long handled spoon or a silicone spatula to mix all ingredients without increasing trace. If desired, add a Tablespoon of finely ground dried lavender buds for gentle exfoliation. Stir gently to distribute the ground lavender evenly throughout the mixture.
7. Pour into mold and decorate the top: Pour the soap mixture into your prepared mold. Tap the mold gently on the counter to remove any air bubbles. Let the batter set up slightly to about the consistency of toothpaste. This may take several minutes. You can use a fork or spoon to add some texture to the top of the mold if desired and sprinkle whole dried lavender buds for decoration if desired. A light line of buds down the center or along one side of the mold is more attractive than covering the whole surface.
8. Insulate and cure: Cover the mold with a lid or cardboard and wrap it in a towel to insulate. Leave the soap undisturbed for 24-48 hours.
9. Unmold and cut: After 18 - 24 hours, check the soap. If using a wooden mold remove inner loaf of soap still enclosed in Parchment of freezer paper or a silicone mold, gently pull a small section of the paper or silicone away from one side. If batter sticks to the paper or mold, set aside for another 24 hours. When the sides come away cleanly, unmold the soap. If it's still soft, let it sit for another day or two before cutting. Once firm, cut the soap into bars using a Stainless-steel knife or soap cutter.
10. Drying: Place the bars on a drying rack in a well-ventilated area. Allow the soap to dry for 4-6 weeks, turning the bars occasionally to ensure even drying.
11. Storage: After drying, store your soap bars in a cool, dry place. Your homemade Lavender Soap is now ready to use!

3. Prepare the Essential Oil Clay Mixture In a glass or stainless-steel container add 30 grams (1.1 ounces) of Tea Tree Essential Oil and 50 grams (1.76 ounces) of French Green Clay. Mix until thoroughly combined. If mixture is too thick add 1 T distilled water and mix until smooth. If you plan to make a two-color soap, evenly divide the essential oil and add half the green clay to that portion and add white kaolin clay to the other portion. Set aside to hydrate.
4. Prepare the oils: Add 209 grams (7.36 ounces) of coconut oil and 150 grams (5.30 ounces) of shea butter in a saucepan (double boiler) or microwave until it reaches the same temperature range as the lye solution (29 - 32°C or 85 - 90°F). Use 30 second bursts in the microwave or low heat in the sauce pan to avoid scorching the oil. Weigh 334 grams (11.78 ounces) of olive oil, 100 grams (3.5 ounces) of avocado oil and 25 grams (1.47 ounces) of castor oil in a separate container. Always add the castor oil last as it is heavy and may stick to the container rather than mixing with the oil if added first.
5. Combine and mix oils Combine the melted oils and butters and the liquid oils in mixing jug. Stick blend to mix oil before adding lye solution.
6. Combine Lye Solution and Oils: Slowly pour the lye solution into the oils while stirring continuously with a spoon or spatula. Use an immersion blender to mix the solution until it reaches thin "trace." This is when the mixture thickens slightly and leaves a visible trail on the surface. Proceed cautiously as adding the clay and essential oil mixture will thicken the batter. If you plan to make a two-color soap, pour off roughly half of the batter into another container.
7. Stir in Essential Oil Clay mixture(s) Hand stir or whisk in the essential oil-clay mixture. Stir slowly and deliberately until fully combined and no different colored swirls are visible in the batter. It should be a uniform color. If you are making a two color soap, mix each clay essential oil mixture into the separate containers.
8. Pour into Mold: Pour the soap mixture into your mold. Tap mold on table to smooth top and bring air bubbles to the surface. If you are making a two-color soap pour in one color, strike on table to flatten and bring air bubbles to the surface than add second color. Using a spoon or chopstick gently mix the two colors together without blending. Both colors should be distinct. Tap the mold gently on the counter to remove any air bubbles. Decorate top as desired.
9. Insulate and Cure: Cover the mold with a lid or cardboard and wrap it in a towel to insulate. Leave the soap undisturbed for 18 -24 hours.
10. Unmold and Cut: After 18 - 24 hours, check the soap. If using a wooden mold remove inner loaf of soap still enclosed in parchment of freezer paper or a silicone mold, gently pull a small section of the paper or silicone away from one side. If batter sticks to the paper or mold, set aside for another 24 hours. When the sides come away cleanly, unmold the soap. If it's still soft, let it sit for another day or two before cutting. Once firm, cut the soap into bars using a knife or soap cutter.
11. Drying: Place the bars on a drying rack in a well-ventilated area. Allow the soap to dry for 4-6 weeks, turning the bars occasionally to ensure even drying.
12. Storage: After drying, store your soap bars in a cool, dry place. Your Green Clay Soap is ready to use.

Cold Process.name: Goat Milk Soap
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Preparation: Prepare your mold for the soap batter. If you are using a wooden mold, line it with freezer paper or parchment paper. Put on safety goggles and gloves. Cover your work area with newspaper or a protective surface. Make sure your equipment is clean and dry.

Weigh 125 grams (4.4 ounces) of distilled water in a heat-resistant container. This is half of the total liquid needed. The other half of the needed liquid will be added as goat milk in the oil mixture. Carefully weigh 122 grams (4.3 ounces) of sodium hydroxide in a separate container. Slowly add the sodium hydroxide to the water (never the other way around) while stirring gently until completely dissolved. The mixture will heat up (as high as 93+ C or 200+ C) and release eye, nose, throat and lung irritating fumes, so do this in a well-ventilated area or under a fume hood. Set the lye solution aside to cool to about 38-43°C (100-110°F). If the lye solution gets too cool, gently warm in a warm tap water bath (add warm to hot tap water in stable pot large enough to accommodate lye jug).
3. Prepare the oils: Weigh 313 grams (11 ounces) of coconut oil, 313 grams (11 ounces) of olive oil, and 209 grams (7.9 ounces) of palm oil into a heat-resistant container. Heat the oils until they reach the same temperature range as the lye-water solution (32-43°C or 90-110°F). You can melt coconut oil and palm oil in microwave in short bursts before adding the olive oil and goat milk to the mixture). Add 122 grams (4.3 ounces) of goat milk to the oil mixture – gently pulse with stick blender to combine oils and milk. Optional: add warm honey and mix well. Check temperature. Set aside to cool if needed or gently heat in 15 second bursts in microwave of too cool. Never re-heat lye solution in the microwave.
4. Combine lye-water solution and oils: When lye solution and oils/goat milk solutions are at the correct temperature (between 90 and 110 and within 10 degrees of each other) slowly pour the lye-water solution into the oils while gently stirring continuously. Use an immersion blender to mix the solution. Stick blend in 5-10 second bursts alternating with stirring with the stick blender or a spatula until it reaches "trace." Trace is achieved when the mixture is completely blended and no more oils float on the batter. The batter thickens and leaves a slightly visible trail or "trace" on the surface when dripped from the blender. It is easy to over blend and make a batter that is too thick.
5. Add essential oils (optional): If you wish to add fragrance, now is the time to mix in your essential oils. Hand-stir well to incorporate without accelerating trace. Stir until no unincorporated oil is visible.
6. Pour into mold: Pour the soap mixture into your mold. If using a wooden mold, make sure it is lined with parchment paper first. Tap the mold gently on the counter by carefully lifting the entire mold about 1.5 cm (1/2 inch) from the counter and allowing to drop gently to remove any air bubbles.
7. Insulate and cure: Cover the mold with a lid or cardboard and wrap it in a towel to insulate. Leave the soap undisturbed for 24-48 hours.

10. Storage: After drying, store your soap bars in a cool, dry place. Your homemade goat milk soap is now ready to use!

3. Prepare the oils: Weigh 443 grams (15.61 ounces) of olive and 58.45 grams (2.1 ounces) of castor oil in a separate container. Always add the castor oil last as it is heavy and may stick to the container rather than mixing with the oil if added first. Add 167 grams (5.89 ounces) of coconut oil and 167 grams (5.89 ounces) of shea butter in a saucepan (double boiler) or microwave until it reaches the same temperature range as the lye solution (29 - 32°C or 85 - 90°F). 4. Combine the melted oils and butters and the liquid oils In a mixing jug stir well to fully mix oils. Add 100 grams (3.5 ounces) of applesauce to oil mixture. Stick blend to mix oil and applesauce before adding lye solution.

This is when the mixture thickens slightly and leaves a visible trail on the surface. Proceed cautiously as the additional sugar from the applesauce may accelerate trace.
6. Pour into Mold: Pour the soap mixture into your mold. If using a wooden mold, line it with parchment paper first. Tap the mold gently on the counter to remove any air bubbles. Decorate top as desired.
7. Insulate and Cure: Cover the mold with a lid or cardboard and wrap it in a towel to insulate. Leave the soap undisturbed for 24-48 hours.
8. Unmold and Cut: After 18 - 24 hours, check the soap. If using a wooden mold remove inner loaf of soap still enclosed in parchment of freezer paper or a silicone mold, gently pull a small section of the paper or silicone away from one side. If batter sticks to the paper or mold, set aside for another 24 hours. When the sides come away cleanly, unmold the soap. If it's still soft, let it sit for another day or two before cutting. Once firm, cut the soap into bars using a knife or soap cutter.
9. Drying: Place the bars on a drying rack in a well-ventilated area. Allow the soap to dry for 4-6 weeks, turning the bars occasionally to ensure even drying.
10. Storage: After drying, store your soap bars in a cool, dry place. Your homemade Apple Soap is now ready to use.

Cold Process.instructions:

3. Prepare the Essential Oils, Yellow Clay, and Turmeric Mixture: Combine 5 grams of Cinnamon Leaf Essential Oil and 5 grams of Clove Bud Essential Oil and 28 grams (1 ounce) of Spice infused olive oil in a glass container, add 2 Tablespoon Yellow Clay and 1.5 teaspoons of Turmeric Powder and blend until smooth. 4. Prepare the oils: Strain and weigh 443 grams (15.61 ounces) of spice infused olive and 58.45 grams (2.1 ounces) of castor oil in a separate container. 6. Combine Lye Solution and Oils: Slowly pour the lye solution into the oils while stirring continuously. Use an immersion blender to mix the solution until it reaches light "trace." This is when the mixture thickens slightly and leaves a visible trail on the surface. Proceed cautiously as the additional sugar from the pumpkin may accelerate trace. More mixing is required to incorporate the essential oils and colorants.

Once firm, cut the soap into bars using a knife or soap cutter.

Cold Process.name: Lavender Garden Soap
Cold Process.instructions:
1. Melt the olive oil, coconut oil, and cocoa butter in a pot over low heat. Bring the temperature to 40-50°C and then turn off the heat.
2. In a separate container, mix sodium hydroxide with distilled water. Carefully mix and ensure good ventilation.
3. Slowly blend the sodium hydroxide solution with the melted oils. Keep the temperature between 35-45°C.
4. Add optional ingredients such as lavender essential oil, rose petals, sage, and oatmeal.
5. Thoroughly mix the ingredients and pour into molds. Use silicone molds sized around 10x10 cm or 4x4 inches.
6. Allow the molds to sit at room temperature for a few days, then remove the soap bars and cut them into desired shapes using a knife soaked in hot water.
7. Let the soap bars cure in a well-ventilated area for a few weeks before use.
8. While pouring the soap mixture into molds, you can decorate the top with rose petals or sage leaves for an elegant and natural touch.
9. Optionally, you can sprinkle oatmeal on top of the soap mixture in the molds to create a textured surface and abstract pattern.
10. Adding lavender essential oil will give the soap bars a pleasant fragrance and a soothing effect. You can also use a few lavender flowers to adorn the tops of the soap bars. Citrus Sunrise Soap

Remedies.name: Relaxation Massage Oil Blend
Remedies.instructions:
1. Add the carrier oil to a clean glass jar.
2. Add the essential oil drops and stir or gently shake to blend - it takes just 2-3 minutes to create your oil blend.
3. Keep the dilution rule of thumb in mind: about three drops of essential oil per teaspoon of carrier oil (a 2% dilution, i.e. 36 drops per 60 ml / 2 oz of carrier oil; up to 4% for acute problems or skin sensitivities).
4. Only make a small batch at a time - the oil smells best when made fresh.
5. Keep at room temperature in a closed glass jar.
6. To warm the massage oil, place the closed glass jar in warm water and test the oil temperature for comfort on your wrist before using.
7. Precautions: do a small patch test before use and discontinue immediately if redness or itching occurs. Do not use on children under two years old, or if you are pregnant (unless directed to by your doctor).
Remedies.source: Soap Academy - 15 Essential Oil Massage Blends
Remedies.benefits: Aromatherapy blend for one full-body massage.

Hair Care.name: Shampoo Bar
Hair Care.instructions:
1. Prepare the guar gum mixture: Measure out cationic guar gum and glycerine. Mix together until the guar gum is fully dispersed.
2. Add oils and panthenol: Measure argan oil, castor oil, and panthenol powder. Add them to the guar/glycerine mixture. Stir well. The panthenol may take time to dissolve—mix and let it sit briefly until no clumps remain.
3. Add preservatives and fragrance: Measure Optiphen, vitamin E oil, and essential oils. Stir into the mixture.
4. Add liquid surfactant and clay: Add cocamidopropyl betaine and kaolin clay. Mix until combined.
5. Safety first: Put on your respirator, safety glasses, gloves, and work in a well-ventilated area.
6. Incorporate the SCI (sodium cocoyl isethionate): Measure the SCI powder. Add to the mixture. Start mixing with a utensil. When it thickens into a dough, switch to kneading with gloved hands until fully combined.
7. Shape the bars: Form by hand or press into a mold. If using a bar press, line it with plastic wrap for easy removal.
8. Cure and store: Let the bars harden for 24 hours before use. Store in a cool, dry place and use within 1 year.
Hair Care.benefits: Mild, creamy-lathering cleanse; kaolin clay absorbs excess scalp oil; glycerin and panthenol attract moisture, strengthen hair, and add shine.

Hair Care.name: Conditioner Bar
ingredients: 2 grams Optiphen Preservative (INCI: Phenoxyethanol (and) Caprylyl Glycol)
Hair Care.instructions:
1. Melt the base ingredients: Weigh murumuru butter, argan oil, BTMS-50, cetyl alcohol, and stearic acid into a heat-safe bowl. Place over a double boiler and heat gently until fully melted.
2. Prepare the glycerine mixture: In a separate bowl, combine glycerine, cationic guar gum, and panthenol powder. Stir until smooth with no clumps. (The panthenol may need to rest in the glycerine for a few minutes to fully dissolve.)
3. Pre-measure the cool-down ingredients: In a small container, weigh out vitamin E oil, Optiphen (preservative), and essential oils. Set aside.
4. Combine mixtures: Once the base (step 1) is fully melted, remove from heat. Stir in the glycerine mixture (step 2) until fully blended. Allow to cool, stirring occasionally and checking the temperature.
5. Add cool-down ingredients: When the mixture reaches below 140°F (60°C), stir in the vitamin E oil, Optiphen, and essential oils. Be careful: If too hot → the preservative may burn off. If too cool → the mixture may solidify before everything blends.
6. Mold and set: Pour the mixture into molds. Place molds in the freezer for 4 hours. This makes it easy to unmold without dents, giving a clean, professional finish.
7. Storage and shelf life: Bars will last up to 1 year if stored away from sunlight and moisture. Once a bar starts touching water, use within 3 months.
